title: phase-gate install plan
description: The installer skill's step-2 output: what it WOULD do, produced before anything is written. This is the recommend-only mode's entire deliverable - verify_citations.py's job is partly to confirm a real plan was produced and read before any --apply step runs, not skipped past.

generated_at.description: When this plan was produced, ISO 8601.

source_commit.description: The phase-gate repo's own git SHA this plan was generated from. Carried through unchanged into the receipt if the adopter proceeds to apply - this is what makes a later update able to tell 'phase-gate changed this' from 'the adopter changed this' (see the build spec's finding 10).

manifest_version.description: The installer/manifest.json schema_version this plan was built against.

adopter_repo_root.description: Absolute path to the adopter's repo root, as detected (git rev-parse --show-toplevel).

variables.description: Every installer/variables.json entry as resolved for this specific adopter - detected, asked, or left at its shipped default.

source.description: How this value was actually arrived at for this install, not just its declared kind. 'left_empty' means the adopter has not actually answered a required-kind question yet - the dependent feature degrades silently and check 2 must fail loudly. 'confirmed_none' means the adopter was asked and confirmed the thing genuinely does not exist for this repo (e.g. no test suite at all) - a deliberate, informed answer, not an unaddressed gap, and check 2 must NOT fail on it.

detection_command.description: Present only when source is 'detected' - the exact command that was run.

components.description: Every component under consideration for this install, ALWAYS one entry per component named in installer/dependencies.json - never one combined entry for a whole shelf. 'Install everything in process/' is a selection convenience the installer offers the adopter, not a different row shape: it just sets every process/ component's status to will_install in the same per-component rows every other selection produces. This matters because check 3 (verify_citations.py) checks hard dependencies by component name - a merged shelf row would make that check meaningless.

status.description: already_present_identical is the idempotent no-op case; already_present_will_update means a diff exists and re-applying will change something.

target_paths.description: Where in the adopter's repo this component's files will land.

prerequisite_note.description: Present only when status is skipped_prerequisite_missing - e.g. review-pr needs a gh remote, implement-queue needs Workflow/worktree support (D3 fail-fast).

citations.description: Every fact this row's verdict actually depends on, both export-side ('this export file says X') and adopter-side ('and that applies to you because Y') - the grounding verify_citations.py's check 1 re-verifies. Can be empty only for a row whose entire verdict is 'ship this file as-is, nothing about it depends on adopter state' - which is rare; most rows should have at least one adopter-side entry.

side.description: Which of the two trusted-as-data-only inputs this citation was read from.

type.description: file_quote grounds a normal claim; command_output is the required form for an absence verdict, which cannot quote a file that doesn't exist.

path.description: Required when type is file_quote - path relative to the side's own root (the export clone, or the adopter repo).

line.description: Optional line number, when type is file_quote.

quote.description: Required when type is file_quote - the actual excerpt read.

command.description: Required when type is command_output - the exact command run.

output.description: Required when type is command_output - its literal output, re-run by verify_citations.py rather than trusted as a stale claim.

repo_files.description: Every entry in installer/manifest.json's repo_files array (methodology.md, PORTING.md, variables.json, the schemas, merge_settings.py, .githooks/*, .gitattributes, .gitignore, LICENSE) - files that are not a 'component' in installer/dependencies.json's sense, but that component text depends on and step 4 requires individual confirmation for (docs/methodology.md above all). Without a row shape here these files had no plan/citation/diff representation at all even though they are load-bearing - see the build spec's T19b finding 2. Same rigor as a components row: grounded citations, not empty by default, and check 1/1b re-verify these exactly like a component.

path.description: Where in the adopter's repo this file lands, matching its manifest.json repo_files entry.

status.description: No skipped_prerequisite_missing here - repo_files have no dependencies.json entry and so no prerequisite to be missing.

class.description: Step 4's risk class this file falls into. docs/methodology.md is always class 4 (standing-authority/rulebook document, individually confirmed - see step 1's conflict check). .githooks/pre-push and scan-secrets.sh are typically class 1 (inert reference prose, once substituted); installer/variables.json is typically class 2 (new adopter-facing file); anything landing in .claude/settings.json goes through merge_settings.py regardless of appearing here.

citations.description: Same shape and same re-verification obligation as a components row's citations - see that field's description above.

conflicts.description: Every conflict merge_settings.py (or any other check) found - e.g. a statusLine already configured differently. Non-empty means --apply cannot proceed cleanly until each is resolved (dropped, or resolved by the adopter) and the plan re-generated.
